title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 676-677 of the continuation of the 'Longue Marche'). Grothendieck works with a group of units mu_ (underlined) in \hat\Gamma_{12}^*, which behaves like (\hat Z)^* with its reduction to (Z/12)^* = {±1, ±5}. He calls the underlying object a 'solution en groupes lisses' over a base S_0. mu is its image in \hat\Gamma_1^*. On the previous page he set nu_2, nu_3 in {0,1}, defined by (-1)^{nu_2} = mu mod 4 and (-1)^{nu_3} = mu mod 6. He then wrote mu_ = (-5)^{nu_2} 5^{nu_3} + 12 nu_0 for a unique section nu_0. This works because -5 ≡ -1 mod 4 and ≡ 1 mod 6, while 5 ≡ 1 mod 4 and ≡ -1 mod 6.

On this page he defines
- (90): nu' = nu_3 - nu_2 - 3 nu_2 nu_3 + 3 nu_0 and nu'' = nu_3 - nu_2 - 2 nu_2 nu_3 + 2 nu_0. The intended sign before 2nu_2nu_3 is minus, as on p. 676.
- (91): mu = eps_2 + 4nu' and mu = eps_3 + 6nu'', with eps_p = (-1)^{nu_p} = 1 - 2nu_p (margin note).
- (91), third line: these combine into a single quantity nu := -nu_2 + 2nu' = -nu_3 + 3nu''.

In modern terms nu' = (mu - eps_2)/4, nu'' = (mu - eps_3)/6 and nu = (mu - 1)/2 in \hat Z. These are the exponents needed to describe how a unit mu (a cyclotomic-character-type parameter) acts on elements of order 4 and 6, the generators of SL_2(Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6. Note that 12 = |SL_2(Z)^ab|.

The NB: mu = 1 is equivalent to nu_2 = nu_3 = nu_0 = 0. Reduction mod 4 and mod 6 kills nu_2 and nu_3, and then 12 nu_0 = 0 forces nu_0 = 0 by torsion-freeness. This implies nu = nu' = nu'' = 0.

The next page uses nu'' to define a group Z~_{rho,sigma} ⊂ O_12^* × M × M by the twisted relation (1-rho)(alpha_0) - (1-sigma)(beta_0) = 3 nu'' lambda_1. This group is an extension of O_12^* related to GL(2, Z/12Z), presumably a model of the normaliser/automorphism data of the profinite modular group.
errors: The cross term is off by a factor 2 when checked against p. 676. There (1+4nu_3)(1-6nu_2) = 1+4nu_3-6nu_2-24nu_2nu_3, so mu = 1+4nu_3-6nu_2+12(nu_0-2nu_2nu_3). Then (91) requires nu' = nu_3-nu_2-6nu_2nu_3+3nu_0 and nu'' = nu_3-nu_2-4nu_2nu_3+2nu_0, not -3nu_2nu_3 and -2nu_2nu_3. Test case nu_2 = nu_3 = 1, nu_0 = 0: mu = -25, but (90)/(91) give -13. Both formulas in (90) are consistent with each other: they correspond to replacing nu_0 by nu_0 - nu_2nu_3. So the third line of (91) and the NB remain valid, and the slip is harmless after renormalising nu_0. Strictly, however, (91) does not follow from (89) as written.
Minor: deducing nu = -nu_2+2nu' = -nu_3+3nu'' from the first two lines of (91) requires dividing by 2, i.e. 2-torsion-freeness of \hat\Gamma_1. This is implicit but fine for \hat Z-like objects.

ideas.what: Decomposition of a unit mu in \hat Z^* via its classes mod 4 and mod 6: mu = eps_2 + 4nu' = eps_3 + 6nu'', with common half-exponent nu = (mu-1)/2.
ideas.modern_name: Exponents (lambda-1)/2, (lambda-eps)/4, (lambda-eps)/6 in the Galois/GT action on finite-order elements of SL_2(Z)^ (Ihara, Drinfeld's m = (lambda-1)/2, Lochak-Nakamura-Schneps)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) for m = (lambda-1)/2 in GT; Ihara, Lochak-Nakamura-Schneps (1990s) for the genus-1 / SL_2 versions

ideas.what: Parametrisation of (Z/12)^* by the signs mod 4 and mod 6 using generators -5 and 5, lifted to \hat\Gamma_{12}^* with a correction 12 nu_0.

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly isolates the quantities nu = (mu-1)/2, nu' = (mu-eps_2)/4 and nu'' = (mu-eps_3)/6. He then uses them (next page) to twist the gluing relation defining an extension of O_12^* attached to the amalgam Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6. These are exactly the exponents later appearing in Drinfeld's and Lochak-Nakamura-Schneps' descriptions of GT acting on torsion elements. Here they are set up in a group-scheme setting ('groupes lisses' over S_0, smooth except in char. 3). This is an independent, apparently unpublished scheme-theoretic anticipation, but the page itself is only bookkeeping.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor historical interest: it shows Grothendieck computing the arithmetic normalisation of the Galois action on the profinite modular group's elliptic elements, in a group-scheme framework. Its novelty lies in the surrounding pages rather than this one.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine arithmetic bookkeeping of unit decompositions mod 4 and mod 6, with a harmless factor-2 slip. Its interest lies only in the context: an anticipation of the GT-type exponents (lambda-1)/2.
transcription_corrections: In (90), second line: the image shows a struck-through symbol before 2nu_2nu_3. The intended sign is '-' (consistent with p. 676 and (87)), not '+'.
Margin note reads: 'si eps_p = (-1)^{nu_p} donc [crossed out] donc eps_p - 1 = -2nu_p (p ∈ {2,3})'. This is consistent with the transcription.
